title: Token tax: LLM token premiums for 200 languages relative to English (FLORES-200)
description:
The same text costs more tokens in most languages compared to English, so speakers of those languages pay more per answer, use up quotas faster, fit less into chat memory and wait longer for answers. Petrov et al. (2023) measured this token premium on the tokenizers of 2023. Most of the models people use today have new tokenizers since then: GPT-4o and GPT-5 (o200k), Gemini 3 and 4, Claude since Opus 4.7, Llama 4, Qwen 3.5. This dataset measures the premium again on those tokenizers, with the same method and text, so the numbers are current, comparable with Petrov et al. and reproducible.

Visualization. Interactive globe built on the data: sara.moricz.se/token-tax.

Languages. All 204 rows of the FLORES-200 devtest split: 196 languages in 29 scripts, 8 of them in two scripts. English is the reference (premium 1.0).

Tokenizers. 13 columns: ChatGPT / Copilot (o200k), GPT-4 2023 (cl100k), Gemini 3.x Flash and Gemini 4 Argon (counted through Google's API), Gemma 3 and Gemma 4, Claude (counted through Anthropic's API), Llama 3 and Llama 4, DeepSeek V3/V4, Qwen 3 and Qwen 3.5, Mistral Tekken. Counted 2026-10-22 to 2026-10-26.

Files. data/data.csv (tokens and premium per language and tokenizer), data/tokenizers.csv (which models use each tokenizer, versions, sources), raw counts in data/counts/, and the scripts that reproduce everything.

Check. The GPT-4 (cl100k) premiums match Petrov et al.'s own counts to a median 0.30 %.
